admission.justification: The decision boundary and the five-category reporting duty are realized in the Manager, Orchestrator, Architect and router texts, and the wording tests assert the exact sentences.

applicability: A Manager or Orchestrator started under the Architect or an Orchestrator, including one whose reporting recipient changed with a second master.
conditions: A matter is categorized under You decide, Send to the Architect, or Send to the developer, or the whole assignment finishes/cannot finish.
An Architect case ruling names only the outcome requiring the Architect and leaves each decision belonging to the Manager with the Manager.
An Orchestrator forwards a Manager's Architect matters unchanged on the same parent route while keeping ordinary sprint operational rulings and requirement readings within the promise.
exclusions: A dashboard-started coordinator, which puts a developer decision in its own chat and invents no parent.
The Architect's retained developer conversation, plan order and requirement texts.

statement: A Manager operates under one explicit three-way boundary: it decides its own execution, construction, precedent-covered matters (a case reservation covers only what it names and never takes back Manager authority), skeletons filling planned gaps, delegated integration, and standing routine paired closeout across all masters including standalone masters; it sends named Architect matters (first reports, qualifying skeletons direct to the Architect, requirement changes, beyond-settings rounds, unconfigured step-ups, second same-kind infrastructure failures, outside-worktree/scratch/task effects, non-routine closeouts, and sprint-line pushes/PRs/main landings/releases) and the five developer-decision categories through its reporting recipient (an assigned Orchestrator forwards Architect matters unchanged, except direct qualifying skeletons); it sends no status-only messages while keeping durable rulings, requirement-change and status records for the Architect to read; and an Architect case ruling names only the outcome needing the Architect while preserving Manager decisions.
title: Manager three-way authority split, Architect rulings and Orchestrator relay
